interpretation: 'If something is moved, it can be otherwise; so if the first actuality is locomotion, then in the respect in which it is moved it can be otherwise, in place, even if not in substance. But since there is something that moves while itself unmoved, being in act, this can in no way be otherwise (τοῦτο οὐκ ἐνδέχεται ἄλλως ἔχειν οὐδαμῶς); for locomotion is the first of changes, and circular locomotion the first of these, and this it causes.' Read as the sentence asserts it: existentially, of the mover whose existence 1072a21-26 has argued ('there is something which moves without being moved', ὃ οὐ κινούμενον κινεῖ). ἀκίνητον is read with that participle as 'not being moved', i.e. moved in no respect (not the modal 'cannot be moved'); ἐνεργείᾳ ὄν as being in act in the respect of being; οὐδαμῶς as every respect (the contrast is with the first heaven, which can be otherwise in place though not in substance). κινεῖ is read in the prima via's broad sense of moving (DISAMB-MOTION): the mover moves as an object of love (1072b3), and the heaven's locomotion is reduced to act for its sake. The reading does not say that every unmoved mover cannot be otherwise (sibling reading -B), that the mover is unique, or that it is pure act; it does not use ἀΐδιον (1072a25, b29) or the necessity of 1072b10-13.
